{
  "schema_version": "gtta.memo@1.0",
  "artifact_id": "us-eu-trade-framework-actor-analysis",
  "title": "US-EU Trade Framework: Actor Leverage Analysis for Mid-Sized Exporters",
  "question": "Who gains and loses leverage from the proposed US-EU trade framework, and what should a mid-sized exporter do next?",
  "decision": "Determine the optimal commercial posture for a mid-sized exporter given shifting leverage among actors in the proposed US-EU trade framework.",
  "audience": "Commercial leadership at a mid-sized exporter evaluating trade-positioning strategy",
  "time_horizon": "6-18 months from framework announcement",
  "mode": "B",
  "evidence_mode": "user-provided sources",
  "confidence": "Moderate",
  "bottom_line": {
    "text": "The proposed US-EU trade framework redistributes leverage primarily toward large-scale incumbents and compliance-ready firms on both sides, while mid-sized exporters face a narrowing window to lock in favorable terms before regulatory harmonization raises the cost of entry. The user-supplied summary indicates tariff reductions in industrial goods but new conformity-assessment requirements that disproportionately burden firms without existing EU or US certification infrastructure. A mid-sized exporter should move now to secure partnerships or certifications rather than wait for final text.",
    "claim_ids": ["c-framework-summary", "c-tariff-reduction", "c-conformity-burden", "c-incumbent-advantage", "c-window-narrowing", "c-action-urgency"]
  },
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim_id": "c-framework-summary",
      "text": "The user-supplied summary of the proposed US-EU trade framework describes a bilateral arrangement covering tariff reductions on industrial goods, mutual recognition of certain standards, and new conformity-assessment requirements for market access.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "user-provided",
      "source_refs": ["user-summary-trade-framework"],
      "confidence": "High"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-tariff-reduction",
      "text": "The framework proposes phased tariff reductions on industrial goods, with the deepest cuts applying to sectors where US and EU producers already compete directly such as machinery, chemicals, and automotive components.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "user-provided",
      "source_refs": ["user-summary-trade-framework"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-conformity-burden",
      "text": "New conformity-assessment provisions would require exporters to obtain certifications from recognized bodies in the destination market, imposing costs that the user summary indicates disproportionately affect firms with annual exports below $50 million.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "user-provided",
      "source_refs": ["user-summary-trade-framework"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-incumbent-advantage",
      "text": "Large incumbents with existing dual-market certification and established compliance teams are positioned to capture the bulk of tariff savings while absorbing conformity costs more easily, increasing their competitive advantage over smaller rivals.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "inference",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-tariff-reduction", "c-conformity-burden"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-eu-regulator-leverage",
      "text": "EU regulatory agencies gain leverage because the conformity model tilts toward the EU's existing CE-marking regime, meaning US exporters must adapt more than EU exporters entering the US market.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "inference",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-framework-summary", "c-conformity-burden"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-us-ag-exclusion",
      "text": "Agricultural products are largely excluded from the framework's tariff provisions, limiting leverage gains for US agricultural exporters and preserving the EU's existing protective posture on food and agriculture.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "user-provided",
      "source_refs": ["user-summary-trade-framework"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-sme-coalition",
      "text": "Industry associations representing small and mid-sized enterprises in both the US and EU have lobbied for transitional periods and fee caps on conformity assessments, but the user summary does not indicate these were included in the current draft.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "inference",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-framework-summary", "c-conformity-burden"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-window-narrowing",
      "text": "The transition period before full conformity requirements take effect is expected to be 18-24 months from ratification, creating a narrowing window during which exporters can secure grandfathered arrangements or early-mover partnerships.",
      "kind": "assumption",
      "provenance": "inference",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-framework-summary"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-action-urgency",
      "text": "A mid-sized exporter that begins certification and partnership processes before the final text is published will face lower costs and less competition for recognized-body capacity than one that waits for ratification.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-conformity-burden", "c-window-narrowing", "c-incumbent-advantage"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "c-third-country-squeeze",
      "text": "Third-country exporters (non-US, non-EU) lose leverage as the bilateral framework may create preferential channels that effectively raise relative tariff and compliance barriers for outsiders.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "inference",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-tariff-reduction", "c-framework-summary"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    }
  ],
  "sections": {
    "actors": {
      "text": "Winners: (1) Large US and EU industrial incumbents gain the most from tariff reductions because they already hold dual-market certifications and can absorb conformity costs, capturing margin improvement directly. (2) EU regulatory agencies gain procedural leverage because the conformity model tilts toward the EU's existing CE-marking approach, meaning US-side adaptation costs are higher. (3) Recognized conformity-assessment bodies on both sides gain revenue and gatekeeping power as demand for their services increases.\n\nLosers: (1) Mid-sized exporters without existing cross-border certifications face disproportionate compliance costs and risk being priced out of the streamlined channel. (2) US agricultural exporters see no leverage gain because agriculture is largely excluded from the tariff provisions. (3) Third-country exporters face a relative disadvantage as the bilateral preference channel raises their effective barriers. (4) SME industry associations have so far failed to secure transitional relief, weakening their negotiating position.\n\nAmbiguous: (1) US trade negotiators secured tariff cuts but conceded on conformity-assessment architecture, making the net leverage shift unclear. (2) EU member-state governments may gain market-access benefits for their firms but lose some regulatory autonomy if mutual-recognition provisions expand in later rounds.",
      "claim_ids": ["c-incumbent-advantage", "c-eu-regulator-leverage", "c-conformity-burden", "c-us-ag-exclusion", "c-third-country-squeeze", "c-sme-coalition", "c-tariff-reduction"]
    }
  },
  "options": [
    {
      "option_id": "opt-early-certify",
      "title": "Begin conformity certification now",
      "benefit": "Locks in recognized-body capacity before demand surges at ratification; potential to grandfather into transitional terms.",
      "downside": "Certification costs are sunk if the framework stalls or conformity provisions change materially in the final text.",
      "conditions": "Appropriate when the exporter's target product categories are clearly within the framework's industrial-goods scope and the user summary's conformity provisions are unlikely to be substantially weakened.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-action-urgency", "c-window-narrowing", "c-conformity-burden"]
    },
    {
      "option_id": "opt-partnership",
      "title": "Secure a distribution or compliance partnership with an incumbent",
      "benefit": "Leverages the incumbent's existing certifications and market access, reducing the exporter's standalone compliance burden.",
      "downside": "Cedes margin and customer relationships to the partner; creates dependency on a firm that may also be a competitor.",
      "conditions": "Suitable when the exporter lacks the scale to justify standalone certification but has differentiated products that an incumbent partner would value.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-incumbent-advantage", "c-conformity-burden"]
    },
    {
      "option_id": "opt-wait",
      "title": "Wait for final legal text before committing resources",
      "benefit": "Avoids sunk costs if the framework changes significantly or fails to be ratified.",
      "downside": "Risks being late to secure certification capacity and partnerships, facing higher costs and longer lead times.",
      "conditions": "Acceptable only if the exporter's current revenue exposure to US-EU trade is low enough that a delayed response would not materially harm competitive position.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-window-narrowing", "c-action-urgency"]
    }
  ],
  "indicators": [
    {
      "indicator_id": "ind-ratification",
      "indicator": "Progress of US-EU framework ratification process",
      "trigger": "Either chamber signals it will fast-track ratification or a committee vote is scheduled within 90 days.",
      "posture_change": "Escalate from monitoring to active certification preparation; the wait-and-see option becomes untenable.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-window-narrowing"]
    },
    {
      "indicator_id": "ind-conformity-text",
      "indicator": "Publication of final conformity-assessment provisions",
      "trigger": "Final text materially changes the conformity model described in the user summary, such as adding SME transitional relief or fee caps.",
      "posture_change": "Reassess the cost-benefit of standalone certification vs. partnership; SME relief would reduce the urgency of the partnership option.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-conformity-burden", "c-sme-coalition"]
    },
    {
      "indicator_id": "ind-rb-capacity",
      "indicator": "Recognized-body appointment and capacity announcements",
      "trigger": "Recognized bodies begin accepting pre-ratification applications or announce capacity constraints.",
      "posture_change": "If capacity is tightening, accelerate the early-certify option; if capacity is ample, the urgency premium decreases.",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["c-action-urgency"]
    }
  ],
  "key_unknowns": [
    "Whether the final legal text will retain, weaken, or strengthen the conformity-assessment provisions described in the user summary.",
    "The actual timeline to ratification and the length of any transitional period.",
    "Whether SME-specific transitional relief or fee caps will be added in the final text.",
    "The capacity and pricing of recognized conformity-assessment bodies once demand materializes."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Analysis is based on a user-supplied summary, not the final legal text; material provisions may change.",
    "No independent verification of the summary's accuracy or completeness was performed.",
    "Sector-specific impacts will vary; this analysis addresses a generic mid-sized industrial exporter rather than a specific product category.",
    "Political risks to ratification (legislative opposition, election cycles, geopolitical shifts) are not modeled."
  ],
  "change_conditions": [
    "The final legal text materially alters the conformity-assessment architecture described in the user summary.",
    "Ratification fails or is indefinitely postponed.",
    "A major geopolitical event (e.g., new tariff escalation, sanctions) disrupts the bilateral negotiating context."
  ]
}

{
  "schema_version": "gtta.memo@1.0",
  "artifact_id": "undersea-cable-damage-ach-b82f67e647714ae1",
  "title": "Analysis of Competing Hypotheses: Undersea Cable Damage Attribution",
  "question": "What explains the observed damage to the undersea cable, and what can be judged without premature attribution given ambiguous vessel movement, weather, and maintenance evidence?",
  "decision": "Whether to attribute cable damage to a specific cause or actor, or to withhold attribution pending further evidence collection.",
  "audience": "Infrastructure security decision-makers and cable operator incident-response teams",
  "time_horizon": "0–6 months from incident detection",
  "mode": "G",
  "evidence_mode": "illustrative source packet",
  "confidence": "Low",
  "bottom_line": {
    "text": "The available evidence is consistent with multiple explanations for the cable damage, and no single hypothesis can be confidently selected over the others. Vessel AIS data shows a commercial bulk carrier transiting the damage zone within the relevant window, but the track is ambiguous—it is consistent with both normal routing and deliberate loitering. Concurrent storm conditions with recorded seabed current velocities above anchor-drag thresholds provide a plausible natural explanation. Maintenance records reveal the cable segment was overdue for inspection by 14 months, introducing degradation as a viable contributor. Premature attribution to sabotage risks misallocation of diplomatic and security resources; premature attribution to natural causes risks under-investing in protection. The bounded judgment is that deliberate interference cannot be ruled out but is not the most probable single explanation on current evidence.",
    "claim_ids": ["C-vessel-ais", "C-weather-storm", "C-maint-overdue", "C-assess-no-single", "C-assess-sabotage-not-ruled-out"]
  },
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim_id": "C-cable-fault",
      "text": "Submarine cable segment KR-7 experienced a complete signal loss at 03:17 UTC on the incident date, with fault localization indicating a break at kilometer marker 342, at a depth of approximately 1,200 meters.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "primary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-cable-operator-fault-report"],
      "confidence": "High"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-damage-profile",
      "text": "Recovery operations found the cable severed with both tensile elongation marks and localized crush damage. The damage pattern does not unambiguously match any single known cause profile (anchor strike, natural abrasion, or deliberate cutting).",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "primary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-recovery-inspection"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-vessel-ais",
      "text": "AIS records show the bulk carrier MV Dorado transited within 1.2 nautical miles of the fault location between 01:40 and 04:55 UTC on the incident date. The vessel's track includes a 47-minute period of reduced speed (2.1 knots) near the damage zone, but this segment also coincides with a course adjustment consistent with the charted traffic separation scheme.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "secondary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-ais-archive"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-vessel-flag",
      "text": "MV Dorado is a Liberian-flagged vessel with a registered owner in a third-country jurisdiction. Open-source shipping databases show no prior incidents involving this vessel.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "secondary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-vessel-registry"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-weather-storm",
      "text": "Meteorological and oceanographic data confirm a force-8 gale transited the area beginning approximately 20:00 UTC the previous day, with modeled near-seabed current velocities of 0.9–1.4 m/s at the cable depth—above the 0.7 m/s threshold commonly associated with anchor drag on soft sediment.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "secondary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-met-ocean-data"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-seabed-geology",
      "text": "The seabed at the fault location is characterized by unconsolidated silt and fine sand, which is susceptible to current-driven sediment mobilization and can expose or undermine buried cable segments during storm events.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "secondary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-seabed-survey"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-maint-overdue",
      "text": "The cable operator's maintenance log shows that the segment including KM 342 was last inspected 26 months before the incident, against a recommended inspection interval of 12 months. Two prior inspection requests were deferred due to budget constraints.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "primary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-maint-log"],
      "confidence": "High"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-no-rov-evidence",
      "text": "No remotely operated vehicle (ROV) survey of the damage site was conducted before recovery operations disturbed the seabed, so forensic evidence of tool marks, anchor gouges, or natural abrasion patterns on the surrounding seabed is unavailable.",
      "kind": "fact",
      "provenance": "primary",
      "source_refs": ["SRC-recovery-inspection"],
      "confidence": "High"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-hyp-sabotage",
      "text": "Hypothesis H1 (deliberate sabotage): A state or non-state actor intentionally severed the cable, potentially using the MV Dorado or an undetected vessel. This hypothesis is consistent with the vessel's proximity and the timing but is not uniquely supported by the evidence: the AIS slow-speed segment is also explained by weather and routing, and the damage profile is inconclusive.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-vessel-ais", "C-damage-profile", "C-no-rov-evidence"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-hyp-anchor",
      "text": "Hypothesis H2 (accidental anchor drag): A vessel—possibly MV Dorado—dragged its anchor across the cable during the storm, causing the damage. This is consistent with weather conditions exceeding anchor-holding thresholds and the vessel's proximity, but there is no confirmation that any vessel deployed an anchor in the area.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-vessel-ais", "C-weather-storm", "C-seabed-geology", "C-damage-profile"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-hyp-natural",
      "text": "Hypothesis H3 (weather and seabed-induced failure): Storm-driven currents mobilized sediment, exposed or undermined the cable, and caused a mechanical failure without any vessel involvement. This is consistent with the storm data and seabed geology, and with the overdue maintenance status, but the crush-damage component of the damage profile is harder to explain by natural forces alone.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-weather-storm", "C-seabed-geology", "C-maint-overdue", "C-damage-profile"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-hyp-degradation",
      "text": "Hypothesis H4 (material degradation): The cable failed due to progressive material fatigue or corrosion exacerbated by deferred maintenance, with the storm acting as a final stressor. This is consistent with the overdue inspection record but does not fully account for the crush damage observed during recovery.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-maint-overdue", "C-damage-profile", "C-weather-storm"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-assess-no-single",
      "text": "No single hypothesis is strongly favored by the current evidence set. Each hypothesis is consistent with some evidence items but inconsistent or silent on others. The absence of pre-recovery seabed forensics is the most significant evidentiary gap.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-hyp-sabotage", "C-hyp-anchor", "C-hyp-natural", "C-hyp-degradation", "C-no-rov-evidence"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-assess-sabotage-not-ruled-out",
      "text": "Deliberate sabotage cannot be excluded on current evidence, but it is not the most probable single explanation. Anchor drag during the storm (H2) and storm-induced natural failure (H3) each have comparable or slightly stronger evidential support because they require fewer unobserved conditions.",
      "kind": "assessment",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-hyp-sabotage", "C-hyp-anchor", "C-hyp-natural", "C-assess-no-single"],
      "confidence": "Low"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-assume-ais-complete",
      "text": "It is assumed that the AIS archive is substantially complete for the area and time window, though AIS transponders can be disabled or spoofed, meaning an undetected vessel presence cannot be excluded.",
      "kind": "assumption",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-vessel-ais"],
      "confidence": "Moderate"
    },
    {
      "claim_id": "C-unknown-tool-marks",
      "text": "Whether the cable damage includes tool marks or cutting signatures that would distinguish deliberate severance from mechanical failure is unknown because no forensic metallurgical analysis has been reported.",
      "kind": "unknown",
      "provenance": "analyst-judgment",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-damage-profile", "C-no-rov-evidence"],
      "confidence": null
    }
  ],
  "sections": {
    "hypotheses": {
      "text": "Four competing hypotheses have been evaluated. H1 (deliberate sabotage) posits intentional cutting by a state or non-state actor, possibly using the transiting MV Dorado as a platform or cover. H2 (accidental anchor drag) posits that a vessel anchor, dragged during the force-8 gale, struck and severed the cable. H3 (storm-induced natural failure) posits that extreme near-seabed currents undermined the cable in its unconsolidated sediment bed without vessel involvement. H4 (material degradation) posits that progressive fatigue or corrosion, compounded by 26 months without inspection, caused failure under storm stress. Each hypothesis can account for some but not all observed evidence.",
      "claim_ids": ["C-hyp-sabotage", "C-hyp-anchor", "C-hyp-natural", "C-hyp-degradation"]
    },
    "evidence_matrix": {
      "text": "The cable fault location and timing (C-cable-fault) are consistent with all four hypotheses and do not discriminate among them. The vessel AIS data (C-vessel-ais) is consistent with H1 and H2 but neutral for H3 and H4—the slow-speed segment is ambiguous. Storm and current data (C-weather-storm, C-seabed-geology) strongly support H2 and H3, are neutral for H4, and neither support nor contradict H1. The overdue maintenance record (C-maint-overdue) supports H3 and H4 and is neutral for H1 and H2. The damage profile (C-damage-profile) is ambiguous across all hypotheses: tensile elongation fits natural failure modes while crush damage is more consistent with anchor impact or deliberate intervention, but none is conclusive. The absence of pre-recovery forensics (C-no-rov-evidence) degrades diagnostic power for every hypothesis. The assumption of AIS completeness (C-assume-ais-complete) is a vulnerability for H1, because a covert actor may have operated without AIS. The unknown metallurgical status (C-unknown-tool-marks) is the single piece of missing evidence most likely to discriminate between deliberate and non-deliberate explanations.",
      "claim_ids": ["C-cable-fault", "C-vessel-ais", "C-weather-storm", "C-seabed-geology", "C-maint-overdue", "C-damage-profile", "C-no-rov-evidence", "C-assume-ais-complete", "C-unknown-tool-marks"]
    },
    "sensitivity": {
      "text": "The analysis is most sensitive to three factors. First, if forensic metallurgical analysis of the recovered cable reveals definitive tool marks or cutting signatures, H1 would be strongly elevated and H3/H4 largely excluded. Second, if port-state or flag-state records confirm that MV Dorado deployed an anchor in the area, H2 would be strongly elevated. Third, if the AIS archive is found to be incomplete—either through transponder manipulation or coverage gaps—the possibility of an undetected vessel raises H1's plausibility. Conversely, if a full ROV survey of the seabed had been conducted before recovery and found no anchor gouges or debris, H2 and H1 would both be weakened. The current inability to test these sensitivities is what prevents confident attribution.",
      "claim_ids": ["C-unknown-tool-marks", "C-vessel-ais", "C-assume-ais-complete", "C-no-rov-evidence"]
    },
    "bounded_judgment": {
      "text": "On current evidence, the most defensible judgment is that the cable damage resulted from a combination of environmental stress and infrastructure vulnerability, with accidental vessel interaction (H2) and storm-induced failure (H3) jointly representing the most probable explanation space. Deliberate sabotage (H1) remains within the range of reasonable hypotheses but requires more unobserved enabling conditions than the alternatives—specifically, an actor with capability, motive, and access, none of which are evidenced. Material degradation (H4) is a plausible contributing factor rather than a standalone explanation. Attribution to any specific actor or intent is not warranted at this time. Decision-makers should invest in forensic metallurgy on the recovered segment and enhanced AIS monitoring of the corridor before revising this judgment.",
      "claim_ids": ["C-assess-no-single", "C-assess-sabotage-not-ruled-out", "C-hyp-anchor", "C-hyp-natural"]
    }
  },
  "key_unknowns": [
    "Whether the cable damage includes tool marks or deliberate cutting signatures (forensic metallurgy not yet performed)",
    "Whether any vessel deployed an anchor in the vicinity during the storm window",
    "Whether the AIS record is complete or whether transponder gaps exist for the area and time window",
    "What the seabed condition was prior to recovery operations disturbing the site"
  ],
  "indicators": [
    {
      "indicator_id": "IND-metallurgy",
      "indicator": "Results of forensic metallurgical analysis on recovered cable segment",
      "trigger": "Analysis report identifies tool marks, clean shear patterns, or other signatures inconsistent with natural mechanical failure",
      "posture_change": "Elevate H1 (sabotage) to primary hypothesis; initiate formal attribution investigation and notify relevant national security authorities",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-unknown-tool-marks", "C-damage-profile"]
    },
    {
      "indicator_id": "IND-anchor-records",
      "indicator": "Port-state or flag-state anchor deployment records for MV Dorado",
      "trigger": "Records confirm anchor deployment within the cable protection zone during the incident window",
      "posture_change": "Elevate H2 (anchor drag) to primary hypothesis; pursue liability and regulatory action against vessel operator",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-vessel-ais", "C-vessel-flag"]
    },
    {
      "indicator_id": "IND-ais-gaps",
      "indicator": "AIS coverage and integrity audit for the incident area and time window",
      "trigger": "Audit reveals transponder gaps, spoofing indicators, or unidentified vessel tracks near the damage zone",
      "posture_change": "Increase plausibility of H1 (sabotage) and re-scope investigation to include covert maritime activity",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-assume-ais-complete", "C-vessel-ais"]
    },
    {
      "indicator_id": "IND-repeat-incident",
      "indicator": "Occurrence of additional cable damage in the same corridor or region",
      "trigger": "A second cable in the same geographic area is damaged within six months under circumstances not fully explained by weather",
      "posture_change": "Significantly elevate H1 (sabotage); treat the corridor as a potential target and escalate to multi-agency investigation",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-hyp-sabotage", "C-assess-sabotage-not-ruled-out"]
    }
  ],
  "options": [
    {
      "option_id": "OPT-withhold-attribution",
      "title": "Withhold attribution and pursue forensic investigation",
      "benefit": "Avoids diplomatic and reputational costs of incorrect attribution; preserves investigative flexibility",
      "downside": "May be perceived as indecisive; delays protective countermeasures if sabotage is the actual cause",
      "conditions": "Forensic metallurgy on recovered segment is commissioned within 30 days; AIS audit is completed within 14 days",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-assess-no-single", "C-unknown-tool-marks"]
    },
    {
      "option_id": "OPT-attribute-natural",
      "title": "Attribute to natural causes and upgrade maintenance regime",
      "benefit": "Enables rapid cable repair without geopolitical escalation; addresses the confirmed maintenance gap",
      "downside": "If sabotage is the true cause, failing to respond invites repeat targeting and signals vulnerability",
      "conditions": "Appropriate only if forensic metallurgy finds no tool marks and AIS audit shows no anomalies",
      "basis_claim_ids": ["C-hyp-natural", "C-maint-overdue", "C-hyp-degradation"]
    },
    {
      "option_id": "OPT-hedged-response",
